comment: FROZEN derivation vectors for ADR-0006 Decision 11a (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#520). Generated by scripts/gen-app-secret-vectors.sh from TWO implementations that share no code with api/internal/appsecret — OpenSSL's HKDF and an RFC 5869 reading in Python checked against the RFC's own Appendix A vectors — which agreed byte for byte. If a code change makes a case here fail, the frozen derivation has changed: add a derivationVersion, do NOT regenerate this file.

cases.why: all-zero seed, a real ULID appID, the first rotation — the plainest case, and the one a re-implementation gets right first
cases.name: db-password

cases.why: all-0xff seed: the seed is used as the HKDF PRK verbatim, so a high-bit-set key is not special-cased anywhere
cases.name: db-password

cases.why: a fixed pseudo-random seed, so the vectors do not all sit on a degenerate key
cases.name: session-key

cases.why: rotation version 2: the version is part of the tuple, so the same (seed, appID, name) at n+1 is a different value
cases.name: session-key

cases.why: version 0xffffffff pins the uint32 BIG-endian encoding of the version; a little-endian writer produces a different value here and an identical one at version 1 only by luck
cases.name: session-key

cases.why: length-prefix injectivity, half one: appID 'a', name 'bc'
cases.name: bc

cases.why: length-prefix injectivity, half two: appID 'ab', name 'c' — concatenation without lengths makes this the same input as half one, and length prefixing is what stops an author-supplied name reaching another app's tuple
cases.name: c

cases.why: a 63-character name, the longest a DNS-1123 label allows, so the name's own length prefix is exercised at its bound
cases.name: abbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbc

cases.why: a one-character name and a one-character appID: the shortest legal tuple
cases.name: k
